chunks: "Electrons are more mobile than holes. In silicon, about 1350 cm²/V·s for electrons versus about 480 for holes at room temperature in lightly doped material, a ratio of roughly 2.
8. The reason is that mobility is q tau over m^ , so it depends on the scattering time and the effective mass.
Electrons in the conduction band have a lighter conductivity effective mass, about 0. 26 times the free electron mass, and a single simple band to move in.
Holes live in the valence band, which has a heavy-hole band and a light-hole band that are degenerate at the top, plus a split-off band nearby.
The heavy-hole band has a larger effective mass, and holes can scatter between these bands, so the average is both heavier and scatters more.
The practical result is that in CMOS the PMOS is made roughly two to three times wider than the NMOS to match the drive current.
NPN transistors are faster and have more gain than PNP of the same process, and N-type resistors have lower resistance than P-type at the same doping.
In other materials the ratio changes: it's about 20 in GaAs, and only about 2 in germanium."
